brief: Modest white-painted gambrel barn of about 1880-1900, roughly 32 ft wide and 36 ft deep, sided in horizontal drop siding with narrow corner boards and a shallow-kicked eave line. The gable end has a centered plank ground-floor door, a hinged plank hay door above it, and a second tall plank door at one corner; no windows on that face. Sits in a mown wheat-stubble field with a small white gable-front garage and a tree line behind.
